name: Peter's denial
charge: Denying Christ three times with cursing and swearing
summary: Though I should die with thee, yet will I not deny thee. Before the cock crew twice he had denied him three times, the last with oaths and curses, to a maid and to bystanders in the high priest's courtyard. The Lord turned and looked upon Peter, and he went out and wept bitterly.
offense: Whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father. Peter did it three times and sealed it with a false oath. The sin was foretold, and so was the mercy: I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
judgment: No sentence but the look and the tears. After the resurrection Christ asked him three times, lovest thou me? and three times restored him: feed my sheep. Peter's godly sorrow worked repentance; Judas' sorrow worked death.

entries.commentary: The feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover. The feast of unleavened bread and the passover are spoken of here as one and the same season.

Then entered Satan into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve. The chief priests and captains were glad, and covenanted to give him money. Men are not in their right mind when they can be glad over a thing like that.
Peter and John are sent to prepare the passover. Christ kept the passover, and a follower of Christ keeps what he kept.

With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer. This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you. Testament and covenant are the same word, and the scripture names who that covenant was made with.
Behold, the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table. He told the rest, while sitting with them, that one of them would do it.

The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors: men who take a benefit for ruling over others. But ye shall not be so. He that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve. As a man is raised in knowledge and understanding he is made more of a servant, not less. I am among you as he that serveth, and he was the greatest of them.
Ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel. The apostles are set to judge the twelve tribes, which is who this word is for.

Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat; but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not; and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren. Peter walked with him and was not yet converted. What converts a man is named in the psalm, and what he strengthens his brethren with is the same thing.
Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death. He is told the cock shall not crow this day, before he shall thrice deny that he knows him.
This that is written must yet be accomplished in me, And he was reckoned among the transgressors. He is quoting the prophets, because the new testament was not yet written when he walked the earth.

Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done. Being in an agony he prayed more earnestly, and his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground. He found them sleeping for sorrow. Grief drains a man and puts him to sleep, and that is what was on them knowing what was coming.

Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss? The servant's ear is cut off and he touches it and heals him. A miracle was done in front of those men in that moment, and they carried him away regardless. This is your hour, and the power of darkness.

Peter denies him three times, and the third time he is known by his speech, for he is a Galilaean. He sounded like the man he was denying. The Lord turned, and looked upon Peter; and Peter remembered the word of the Lord, and went out, and wept bitterly.

The men that held him mocked him and smote him, and blindfolded him. Hereafter shall the Son of man sit on the right hand of the power of God. Art thou then the Son of God? And he said, Ye say that I am.

Christ calls the twelve and gives them power against unclean spirits and to heal all manner of sickness and disease, the same works he was doing himself. The twelve are named here, ending with Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The twelve go to the southern kingdom first, before the gospel goes to the northern kingdom.
Preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils. Freely ye have received, freely give.
They are to carry no gold, silver or brass, no scrip, no second coat, no shoes, no staves, for the workman is worthy of his meat.
In every city they are to enquire who in it is worthy, and to let their peace rest on a worthy house and return to them from one that is not.
Where they are not received they shake off the dust of their feet, and it shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment than for that city.

Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. This is a word for a people living in captivity. There is only so much that can be said and done on another man's ground, and wisdom is required alongside harmlessness.

They will be delivered up to the councils and scourged in the synagogues, which is what the Pharisees had the power to do. They are brought before governors and kings for a testimony against them and the Gentiles: against their own people who turned on Christ, and against the rulers of that time.
Take no thought how or what ye shall speak, for it shall be given you in that same hour. It is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

The brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child. Serving the Most High brings division, and it comes first inside your own house. Ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
When they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another.
The disciple is not above his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, they will call them of his household worse.
There is nothing covered that shall not be revealed. What is told in darkness is to be spoken in light, and what is heard in the ear preached upon the housetops.
Fear not them which kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Not one sparrow falls to the ground without your Father, and the very hairs of your head are all numbered. That is not written for decoration; it is how closely he holds his own.
Whosoever shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father; and whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny.
I came not to send peace, but a sword. A man's foes shall be they of his own household.

He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. This is not forbidding natural love for your family; it is forbidding the trimming of your ways to keep peace with them. That is how the pagan holidays come back in. A brother in the truth goes to see family he has not seen in a long while, and he sits down in the feast to keep them comfortable.

He that taketh not his cross and followeth after me is not worthy of me. He that findeth his life shall lose it, and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it. What is given up is the sin that was being lived in. That old man is put to death, and the life that is found is coming out of the congregation of the dead.

He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me. Even a cup of cold water given in the name of a disciple does not lose its reward, and the reward in view is the kingdom.

verses.text: Peter answered and said unto him, Though all men shall be offended because of thee, yet will I never be offended.
Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
Peter said unto him, Though I should die with thee, yet will I not deny thee. Likewise also said all the disciples.
Now Peter sat without in the palace: and a damsel came unto him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galilee.
But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what thou sayest.
And when he was gone out into the porch, another maid saw him, and said unto them that were there, This fellow was also with Jesus of Nazareth.
And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.
And after a while came unto him they that stood by, and said to Peter, Surely thou also art one of them; for thy speech bewrayeth thee.
Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew.
And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.
And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat:
But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
And he said unto him, Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.
And he said, I tell thee, Peter, the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.
And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.
And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.
He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep.

He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.
For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
And as Peter was beneath in the palace, there cometh one of the maids of the high priest:
And when she saw Peter warming himself, she looked upon him, and said, And thou also wast with Jesus of Nazareth.
But he denied, saying, I know not, neither understand I what thou sayest. And he went out into the porch; and the cock crew.
And a maid saw him again, and began to say to them that stood by, This is one of them.
And he denied it again. And a little after, they that stood by said again to Peter, Surely thou art one of them: for thou art a Galilean, and thy speech agreeth thereto.
But he began to curse and to swear, saying, I know not this man of whom ye speak.
And the second time the cock crew. And Peter called to mind the word that Jesus said unto him, Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. And when he thought thereon, he wept.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not lie to one another.
You shall not swear by God's name falsely.
We should avoid making any oaths so that you may not fall under judgment.
True repentance is evidenced by one's fruits.
